statements.label: supported
statements.text: The study reported the birth of six healthy cloned calves derived from senescent donor somatic cells.
statements.evidence: we report the birth of six healthy cloned calves derived from populations of senescent donor somatic cells
statements.note: The abstract states six healthy cloned calves were born from senescent donor cells.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Telomere elongation in the cloned cells was driven by reactivation of telomerase.
statements.evidence: Southern blot and flow cytometric analyses indicated that the telomeres were also extended beyond those of newborn (<2 weeks old) and age-matched control animals.
statements.note: The abstract reports telomeres were extended but never identifies telomerase or any underlying mechanism.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: EPC-1 expression in the cloned animals' cells ran 3.5- to 5-fold higher than in age-matched control cells.
statements.evidence: Early population doubling level complementary DNA-1 (EPC-1, an age-dependent gene) expression in cells from the cloned animals was 3.5- to 5-fold higher than that in cells from age-matched (5 to 10 months old) controls.
statements.note: The abstract gives the 3.5- to 5-fold higher EPC-1 expression over age-matched controls.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Nuclear transfer lengthened senescent cells' replicative life-span from a few doublings to more than 90 population doublings.
statements.evidence: Nuclear transfer extended the replicative life-span of senescent cells (zero to four population doublings remaining) to greater than 90 population doublings.
statements.note: The abstract states nuclear transfer extended the life-span from zero-to-four to over 90 doublings.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Cholesterol crystals activated the NLRP3 inflammasome in phagocytes in vitro through a process involving phagolysosomal damage.
statements.evidence: cholesterol crystals activate the NLRP3 inflammasome in phagocytes in vitro in a process that involves phagolysosomal damage
statements.note: The abstract directly reports this in vitro activation involving phagolysosomal damage.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Minute cholesterol crystals appear in early atherosclerotic lesions, coinciding with the first appearance of inflammatory cells in mice.
statements.evidence: minute cholesterol crystals are present in early diet-induced atherosclerotic lesions and that their appearance in mice coincides with the first appearance of inflammatory cells
statements.note: The abstract reports crystals in early lesions coinciding with the first inflammatory cells.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: LDLR-deficient mice given inflammasome-deficient bone marrow on a high-cholesterol diet showed markedly decreased early atherosclerosis.
statements.evidence: they had markedly decreased early atherosclerosis and inflammasome-dependent IL-18 levels
statements.note: The abstract states these transplanted mice had markedly decreased early atherosclerosis.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Inhibiting interleukin-1 lowers the rate of cardiovascular events in patients with atherosclerosis.
statements.evidence: These findings provide new insights into the pathogenesis of atherosclerosis and indicate new potential molecular targets for the therapy of this disease.
statements.note: The abstract only points to potential molecular targets and reports no clinical or patient outcomes.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Scavenging reactive oxygen species with antioxidants prevents NLRP3 inflammasome activation in living animals.
statements.evidence: These results provide a missing link between apoptosis and inflammasome activation, via binding of cytosolic oxidized mtDNA to the NLRP3 inflammasome.
statements.note: The abstract describes the molecular link in cells but tests no antioxidant intervention in vivo.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: With NF-κB signal 1 present, mitochondrial apoptotic signaling activated the NLRP3 inflammasome and licensed interleukin-1β production.
statements.evidence: in the presence of signal 1 (NF-κB), the NLRP3 inflammasome was activated by mitochondrial apoptotic signaling that licensed production of interleukin-1β (IL-1β)
statements.note: The abstract states this directly as its opening finding.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Macrophages lacking mitochondrial DNA showed severely attenuated IL-1β production yet still underwent apoptosis.
statements.evidence: macrophages lacking mtDNA had severely attenuated IL-1β production, yet still underwent apoptosis
statements.note: The abstract reports severely attenuated IL-1β production despite intact apoptosis in mtDNA-lacking macrophages.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The antiapoptotic protein Bcl-2 inversely regulated mitochondrial dysfunction and NLRP3 inflammasome activation.
statements.evidence: The antiapoptotic protein Bcl-2 inversely regulated mitochondrial dysfunction and NLRP3 inflammasome activation.
statements.note: The abstract states Bcl-2 inversely regulated both mitochondrial dysfunction and inflammasome activation.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Necrotic cells were sensed by the Nlrp3 inflammasome, leading to release of the proinflammatory cytokine IL-1beta.
statements.evidence: necrotic cells are sensed by the Nlrp3 inflammasome resulting in the subsequent release of the proinflammatory cytokine IL-1beta
statements.note: The abstract directly reports necrotic-cell sensing by Nlrp3 and IL-1beta release.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Nlrp3 inflammasome activation was triggered partly by ATP produced from mitochondria released by damaged cells.
statements.evidence: Nlrp3 inflammasome activation was triggered in part through ATP produced by mitochondria released from damaged cells.
statements.note: The abstract states activation was triggered in part through mitochondria-derived ATP.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Pharmacologically blocking Nlrp3 reduced inflammation in human kidney transplant recipients.
statements.evidence: These findings suggest that the inhibition of Nlrp3 inflammasome activity can diminish the acute inflammation and damage associated with tissue injury.
statements.note: The abstract suggests inhibition could help but reports only animal models, no human data.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Neutrophil influx into the peritoneum after necrotic-cell exposure was markedly diminished when Nlrp3 was absent.
statements.evidence: Neutrophilic influx into the peritoneum in response to necrotic cells in vivo was also markedly diminished in the absence of Nlrp3.
statements.note: The abstract reports neutrophil influx was markedly diminished without Nlrp3.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: CD36 drove an endocytic pathway converting soluble ligands into crystals or fibrils, causing lysosomal disruption and NLRP3 inflammasome activation.
statements.evidence: an endocytic pathway mediated by the pattern-recognition receptor CD36 that coordinated the intracellular conversion of those soluble ligands into crystals or fibrils, which resulted in lysosomal disruption and activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome
statements.note: The abstract describes exactly this CD36-mediated conversion and resulting inflammasome activation.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Pharmacological CD36 inhibitors improve cognition in patients with Alzheimer's disease.
statements.evidence: Particulate ligands, including cholesterol crystals and amyloid fibrils, induce production of interleukin 1β (IL-1β) dependent on the cytoplasmic sensor NLRP3 in atherosclerosis, Alzheimer's disease and diabetes.
statements.note: The abstract lists Alzheimer's as a context but reports no cognitive or patient outcomes.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Targeting CD36 in atherosclerotic mice produced lower serum IL-1β and reduced cholesterol crystal accumulation in plaques.
statements.evidence: targeting CD36 in atherosclerotic mice resulted in lower serum concentrations of IL-1β and accumulation of cholesterol crystals in plaques
statements.note: The abstract reports targeting CD36 gave lower serum IL-1β and less crystal accumulation in plaques.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: CD36 acts as a central regulator of inflammasome activation in sterile inflammation.
statements.evidence: position CD36 as a central regulator of inflammasome activation in sterile inflammation
statements.note: The abstract concludes by positioning CD36 as a central regulator of inflammasome activation.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Calorie restriction and exercise-driven weight loss in obese type 2 diabetics reduced adipose Nlrp3 expression and improved insulin sensitivity.
statements.evidence: calorie restriction and exercise-mediated weight loss in obese individuals with type 2 diabetes is associated with a reduction in adipose tissue expression of Nlrp3 as well as with decreased inflammation and improved insulin sensitivity
statements.note: The abstract links this weight loss to reduced Nlrp3, less inflammation and improved insulin sensitivity.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The Nlrp3 inflammasome sensed lipotoxicity-associated rises in intracellular ceramide to drive caspase-1 cleavage in macrophages and adipose tissue.
statements.evidence: the Nlrp3 inflammasome senses lipotoxicity-associated increases in intracellular ceramide to induce caspase-1 cleavage in macrophages and adipose tissue
statements.note: The abstract states Nlrp3 senses ceramide increases to induce caspase-1 cleavage.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Pharmacologic NLRP3 inhibitors improve glycemic control in patients with type 2 diabetes.
statements.evidence: Collectively, these data establish that the Nlrp3 inflammasome senses obesity-associated danger signals and contributes to obesity-induced inflammation and insulin resistance.
statements.note: The abstract shows Nlrp3 contributes to insulin resistance but tests no NLRP3-inhibiting drug in patients.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Eliminating Nlrp3 in obese mice lowered IL-18 and IFN-γ, raised naive T cell numbers, and cut effector T cells.
statements.evidence: elimination of Nlrp3 in obese mice reduces IL-18 and adipose tissue interferon-γ (IFN-γ) expression, increases naive T cell numbers and reduces effector T cell numbers in adipose tissue
statements.note: The abstract reports these reductions in IL-18, IFN-γ and effector T cells and the rise in naive T cells.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Caspase-1 rose during adipocyte differentiation and pushed adipocytes toward a more insulin-resistant phenotype.
statements.evidence: Caspase-1 is upregulated during adipocyte differentiation and directs adipocytes toward a more insulin-resistant phenotype.
statements.note: The abstract states caspase-1 is upregulated during differentiation and drives a more insulin-resistant phenotype.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Caspase-1-deficient mice were more insulin sensitive than wild-type animals.
statements.evidence: mice deficient in caspase-1 are more insulin sensitive as compared to wild-type animals
statements.note: The abstract directly reports caspase-1-deficient mice as more insulin sensitive than wild-type.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Indirect calorimetry showed higher fat oxidation rates in caspase-1-knockout animals.
statements.evidence: Indirect calorimetry analysis revealed higher fat oxidation rates in caspase-1(-/-) animals.
statements.note: The abstract reports higher fat oxidation rates in caspase-1 knockouts by calorimetry.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Blocking caspase-1 lowers fasting blood glucose in human patients with type 2 diabetes.
statements.evidence: In vivo, treatment of obese mice with a caspase-1 inhibitor significantly increases their insulin sensitivity.
statements.note: The abstract reports caspase-1 inhibition only in mice, with no human patient data.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Alu RNA activates the NLRP3 inflammasome through release of mitochondrial DNA.
statements.evidence: The mechanism of Alu RNA-induced cytotoxicity is unknown.
statements.note: The abstract reports NLRP3 activation but never identifies the upstream trigger, so the mtDNA route is neither stated nor ruled out.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: DICER1 deficiency or Alu RNA exposure activated the NLRP3 inflammasome and triggered TLR-independent MyD88 signaling via IL18 in the RPE.
statements.evidence: DICER1 deficit or Alu RNA exposure activates the NLRP3 inflammasome and triggers TLR-independent MyD88 signaling via IL18 in the RPE
statements.note: The abstract states this activation and TLR-independent MyD88 signaling directly.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Inhibiting inflammasome components, MyD88, or IL18 prevented RPE degeneration caused by DICER1 loss or Alu RNA exposure.
statements.evidence: Genetic or pharmacological inhibition of inflammasome components (NLRP3, Pycard, Caspase-1), MyD88, or IL18 prevents RPE degeneration induced by DICER1 loss or Alu RNA exposure
statements.note: The abstract reports that inhibiting these components prevents the RPE degeneration.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Human geographic atrophy RPE contained elevated NLRP3, PYCARD, and IL18 with increased caspase-1 and MyD88 activation.
statements.evidence: human GA RPE contains elevated amounts of NLRP3, PYCARD, and IL18 and evidence of increased Caspase-1 and MyD88 activation
statements.note: The abstract reports elevated NLRP3, PYCARD and IL18 and increased caspase-1 and MyD88 activation in human GA RPE.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Myeloma cells exposed to low-dose doxorubicin, melphalan, or bortezomib up-regulated DNAM-1 and NKG2D ligands.
statements.evidence: myeloma cells treated with low doses of therapeutic agents commonly used in the management of patients with MM, such as doxorubicin, melphalan, and bortezomib, up-regulate DNAM-1 and NKG2D ligands
statements.note: The abstract reports these low-dose drugs up-regulate DNAM-1 and NKG2D ligands.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Combining these drugs with NK-cell infusions improves clinical outcomes in multiple myeloma patients.
statements.evidence: There is much evidence to support a role for natural killer (NK) cells in controlling the progression of multiple myeloma (MM), a malignancy characterized by an abnormal plasma cell proliferation in the bone marrow (BM).
statements.note: The abstract studies ligand regulation in cell lines and ex vivo cells but reports no patient clinical outcomes.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Drug treatment of myeloma cells increased NK-cell degranulation, with NKG2D and DNAM-1 as the major triggering receptors.
statements.evidence: therapeutic drug treatment of MM cells increases NK-cell degranulation, the NKG2D and DNAM-1 receptors being the major triggering molecules
statements.note: The abstract reports drug treatment increases NK degranulation via NKG2D and DNAM-1.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The ATM and ATR inhibitors caffeine and KU-55933 abolished the drug-induced DNAM-1 and NKG2D ligand expression.
statements.evidence: Drug-induced DNAM-1 and NKG2D ligand expression was abolished after treatment with the ATM (ataxia telangiectasia mutated) and ATR (ATM- and RAD3-related) pharmacologic inhibitors caffeine and KU-55933
statements.note: The abstract reports the ATM/ATR inhibitors caffeine and KU-55933 abolished the drug-induced ligand expression.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Active caspase-1 expression was strongly enhanced in human mild cognitive impairment and Alzheimer's disease brains.
statements.evidence: we demonstrate strongly enhanced active caspase-1 expression in human mild cognitive impairment and brains with Alzheimer's disease
statements.note: The abstract reports strongly enhanced active caspase-1 in human MCI and Alzheimer's brains.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Knockout mice carrying familial-Alzheimer's mutations were largely protected from loss of spatial memory and other disease sequelae.
statements.evidence: mice carrying mutations associated with familial Alzheimer's disease were largely protected from loss of spatial memory and other sequelae associated with Alzheimer's disease
statements.note: The abstract reports these Nlrp3- and Casp1-knockout mice were largely protected from spatial memory loss and other sequelae.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: NLRP3 deficiency skewed microglia toward an M2 phenotype and decreased amyloid-β deposition in the APP/PS1 model.
statements.evidence: NLRP3 inflammasome deficiency skewed microglial cells to an M2 phenotype and resulted in the decreased deposition of amyloid-β in the APP/PS1 model of Alzheimer's disease
statements.note: The abstract reports NLRP3 deficiency drove an M2 microglial phenotype and decreased amyloid-β deposition.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Pharmacological NLRP3 inhibition reverses established memory deficits in Alzheimer's disease patients.
statements.evidence: These results show an important role for the NLRP3/caspase-1 axis in the pathogenesis of Alzheimer's disease, and suggest that NLRP3 inflammasome inhibition represents a new therapeutic intervention for the disease.
statements.note: The abstract suggests NLRP3 inhibition as a therapeutic intervention but tests only mice, not patients.
